vsm2.13:41.1: After that, at the end of a long period, a seventh sun appears.
vsm2.13:41.2: And when that has appeared, the whole world-sphere together with the hundred thousand million other world-spheres catches fire.
vsm2.13:41.3: Even the summits of Sineru, a hundred leagues and more high, crumble and vanish into space.
vsm2.13:41.4: The conflagration mounts up and invades the realm of the Four Kings.
vsm2.13:41.5:
When it has burnt up all the golden palaces, the jewelled palaces and the crystal
palaces there, it invades the Realm of the Thirty-three.
vsm2.13:41.6: And so it goes right on up to the plane of the first jhāna.
vsm2.13:41.7: When it has burnt three lower Brahmā-worlds, it stops there at the Ābhassara-world.
vsm2.13:41.8: As long as any formed thing (formation) the size of an atom still exists it does not go out;
vsm2.13:41.9: but it goes out when all formed things have been consumed. And like the flame that burns ghee and oil, it leaves no ash.
vsm2.13:42.1: The upper space is now all one with the lower space in a vast gloomy darkness.
vsm2.13:42.2: Then at the end of a long period a great cloud arises, and at first it rains gently,
vsm2.13:42.3:
and then it rains with ever heavier deluges, like lotus stems, like rods, like pestles, like palm trunks,
more and more. And so it pours down upon all burnt areas in the hundred thousand million world-spheres till they disappear.
vsm2.13:42.4: Then the winds (forces) beneath and all around that water rise up and compact it and round it, like water drops on a lotus leaf.
vsm2.13:42.5: How do they compact the great mass of water?
vsm2.13:42.6: By making gaps; for the wind makes gaps in it here and there.
vsm2.13:43.1: Being thus compressed by the air, compacted and reduced, it gradually subsides.
vsm2.13:43.2:
As it sinks, the lower Brahmā-world reappears in its place, and worlds divine
reappear in the places of the four upper divine worlds of the sensual sphere.
vsm2.13:43.3: But when it has sunk to the former earth’s level, strong winds (forces) arise
vsm2.13:43.4: and they stop it and hold it stationary, like the water in a water pot when the outlet is plugged.
vsm2.13:43.5: As the fresh water gets used up, the essential humus makes its appearance on it.
vsm2.13:43.6: That possesses colour, smell and taste, like the surface film on milk rice when it dries up.
vsm2.13:44.1:
Then the beings that were reborn first in the Brahmā-world of Streaming-radiance (Ābhassara)
fall from there with the exhaustion of their life span, or when their merit is exhausted, and they reappear here.
vsm2.13:44.2: They are self-luminous and wander in the sky.
vsm2.13:44.3:
On eating the essential humus, as is told in the Aggañña Sutta (D III 85), they
are overcome by craving, and they busy themselves in making lumps of it to eat.
vsm2.13:44.4: Then their self-luminosity vanishes, and it is dark.
vsm2.13:44.5: They are frightened when they see the darkness.
vsm2.13:45.1: Then in order to remove their fears and give them courage, the sun’s disk appears full fifty leagues across.
vsm2.13:45.2: They are delighted to see it, thinking, “We have light,”
vsm2.13:45.3:
and they say, “It has appeared in order to allay our fears and give us courage (sūrabhāva),
so let it be called ‘sun’ (suriya).” So they give it the name “sun” (suriya).
vsm2.13:45.4: Now, when the sun has given light for a day, it sets. Then they are frightened again, thinking, “We have lost the light we had,”
vsm2.13:45.5: and they think, “How good if we had another light!”
vsm2.13:46.1: As if knowing their thought, the moon’s disk appears, forty-nine leagues across.
vsm2.13:46.2:
On seeing it they are still more delighted, and they say, “It has appeared, seeming as if it knew our desire
(chanda), so let it be called ‘moon’ (canda).” So they give it the name “moon” (canda).
vsm2.13:47.1: After the appearance of the moon and sun in this way, the stars appear in their constellations.
vsm2.13:47.2: After that, night and day are made known, and in due course, the month and half month, the season, and the year.
vsm2.13:48.1: On the day the moon and sun appear, the mountains of Sineru, of the World-sphere and of Himalaya appear too.
vsm2.13:48.2: And they appear on the full-moon day of the month of Phagguna (March), neither before nor after.
vsm2.13:48.4: Just as, when millet is cooking and bubbles arise, then simultaneously, some parts are domes, some hollow, and some flat,
vsm2.13:48.5: so too, there are mountains in the domed places, seas in the hollow places, and continents (islands) in the flat places.
vsm2.13:49.1: Then, as these beings make use of the essential humus, gradually some become handsome and some ugly.
vsm2.13:49.2: The handsome ones despise the ugly ones.
vsm2.13:49.3: Owing to their contempt the essential humus vanishes
vsm2.13:49.4: and an outgrowth from the soil appears.
vsm2.13:49.5: Then that vanishes in the same way
vsm2.13:49.7: That too vanishes in the same way
vsm2.13:49.8: and the rice without red powder or husk that ripens without tilling appears, a clean sweet-smelling rice fruit.
vsm2.13:50.2: These beings put the rice into the vessels, which they put on the tops of stones. A flame appears spontaneously and cooks it.
vsm2.13:50.3: The cooked rice resembles jasmine flowers. It has no need of sauces and curries,
vsm2.13:50.4: since it has whatever flavour they want to taste.
vsm2.13:51.1: As soon as they eat this gross food, urine and excrement appear in them.
vsm2.13:51.2: Then wound orifices break open in them to let these things out. The male sex appears in the male, and the female sex in the female.
vsm2.13:51.3: Then the females brood over the males, and the males over the females for a long time.
vsm2.13:51.4: Owing to this long period of brooding, the fever of sense desires arises.
vsm2.13:51.5: After that they practice sexual intercourse.
vsm2.13:52.1:
For their overt practice of evil they are censured and punished by the wise, and so
they build houses for the purpose of concealing the evil.
vsm2.13:52.2: When they live in houses, they eventually fall in with the views of the more lazy, and they make stores of food.
vsm2.13:52.3:
As soon as they do that, the rice becomes enclosed in red powder and husks and no longer
grows again of itself in the place where it was reaped.
vsm2.13:52.4:
They meet together and bemoan the fact, “Evil has surely made its appearance among beings; for formerly we
were mind-made …” (D III 90), and all this should be given in full in the way described in the Aggañña Sutta.
vsm2.13:53.1: After that, they set up boundaries.
vsm2.13:53.2: Then some being takes a portion given to another.
vsm2.13:53.3: After he has been twice rebuked, at the third time they come to blows with fists, clods, sticks, and so on.
vsm2.13:53.4: When stealing, censuring, lying, resorting to sticks, etc., have appeared in this way, they meet together, thinking,
vsm2.13:53.5:
“Suppose we elect a being who would reprove those who should be reproved, censure those who should be censured, and banish
those who should be banished, and suppose we keep him supplied with a portion of the rice?” (D III 92).
vsm2.13:54.1:
When beings had come to an agreement in this way in this aeon, firstly this Blessed One himself,
who was then the Bodhisatta (Being due to be Enlightened), was the handsomest, the most comely,
the most honourable, and was clever and capable of exercising the effort of restraint.
vsm2.13:54.2: They approached him, asked him, and elected him.
vsm2.13:54.3: Since he was recognized (sammata) by the majority (mahā-jana) he was called Mahā Sammata.
vsm2.13:54.4: Since he was lord of the fields (khetta) he was called khattiya (warrior noble).
vsm2.13:54.5:
Since he promoted others’ good (rañjeti) righteously and equitably he was a king (rājā).
This is how he came to be known by these names.
vsm2.13:54.6: For the Bodhisatta himself is the first man concerned in any wonderful innovation in the world.
vsm2.13:54.7:
So after the khattiya circle had been established by making the Bodhisatta the first in this way,
the brahmans and the other castes were founded in due succession.
vsm2.13:55.1:
Herein, the period from the time of the great cloud heralding the aeon’s destruction up till
the ceasing of the flames constitutes one incalculable, and that is called the “contraction.”
vsm2.13:55.2:
That from the ceasing of the flames of the aeon destruction up till the great cloud of rehabilitation, which rains down upon the
hundred thousand million world-spheres, constitutes the second incalculable, and that is called, “what supersedes the contraction.”
vsm2.13:55.3:
That from the time of the great cloud of rehabilitation up till the appearance of the moon and sun
constitutes the third incalculable, and that is called the “expansion.”
vsm2.13:55.4:
That from the appearance of the moon and sun up till the reappearance of the great cloud of the aeon
destruction is the fourth incalculable, and that is called, “what supersedes the expansion.”
vsm2.13:55.5: These four incalculables make up one great aeon.
vsm2.13:55.6: This, firstly, is how the destruction by fire and reconstitution should be understood.
vsm2.13:56.1:
The occasion when the aeon is destroyed by water should be treated in the way already described beginning,
“First of all a great cloud heralding the aeon’s destruction appears …” (§32).
vsm2.13:57.1:
There is this difference, however. While in the former case a second sun appeared, in this
case a great cloud of caustic waters appears.
vsm2.13:57.2:
At first it rains very gently, but it goes on to rain with gradually greater deluges,
pouring down upon the hundred thousand million world-spheres.
vsm2.13:57.3:
As soon as they are touched by the caustic waters, the earth, the mountains, etc.,
melt away, and the waters are supported all round by winds.
vsm2.13:57.4: The waters take possession from the earth up to the plane of the second jhāna.
vsm2.13:57.5: When they have dissolved away the three Brahmā-worlds there, they stop at the Subhakiṇha-world.
vsm2.13:57.6: As long as any formed thing the size of an atom exists they do not subside;
vsm2.13:57.7: but they suddenly subside and vanish away when all formed things have been overwhelmed by them.
vsm2.13:57.8: All beginning with: “The upper space is all one with the lower space in a vast gloomy darkness …” (§42) is as already described,
vsm2.13:57.9: except that here the world begins its reappearance with the Ābhassara Brahmā-world.
vsm2.13:57.10: And beings falling from the Subhakiṇha Brahmā-world are reborn in the places beginning with the Ābhassara Brahmā-world.
vsm2.13:58.1:
Herein, the period from the time of the great cloud heralding the aeon’s destruction up till
the ceasing of the aeon-destroying waters constitutes one incalculable.
vsm2.13:58.2: That from the ceasing of the waters up till the great cloud of rehabilitation constitutes the second incalculable.
vsm2.13:58.3: That from the great cloud of rehabilitation … These four incalculables make up one great aeon.
vsm2.13:58.4: This is how the destruction by water and reconstitution should be understood.
vsm2.13:59.1:
The occasion when the aeon is destroyed by air should be treated in the way already described
beginning with the “first of all a great cloud heralding the aeon’s destruction appears …” (§32).
vsm2.13:60.1: There is this difference, however. While in the first case there was a second sun, here a wind arises in order to destroy the aeon.
vsm2.13:60.2: First of all it lifts up the coarse flue,
vsm2.13:60.3:
then the fine flue, then the fine sand, coarse sand, gravel, stones, etc., until it lifts up
stones as big as a catafalque, and great trees standing in uneven places.
vsm2.13:60.4: They are swept from the earth up into the sky, and instead of falling down again
vsm2.13:60.5: they are broken to bits there and cease to exist.
vsm2.13:61.1: Then eventually wind arises from underneath the great earth and overturns the earth, flinging it into space.
vsm2.13:61.2:
The earth splits into fragments measuring a hundred leagues, measuring two, three, four, five hundred
leagues, and they are hurled into space too, and there they are broken to bits and cease to exist.
vsm2.13:61.3: The world-sphere mountains and Mount Sineru are wrenched up and cast into space,
vsm2.13:61.4: where they crash against each other till they are broken to bits and disappear.
vsm2.13:61.5:
In this way it destroys the divine palaces built on the earth of Mount Sineru and those built in space,
it destroys the six sensual-sphere divine worlds, and it destroys the hundred thousand million world-spheres.
vsm2.13:61.6:
Then world-sphere collides with world-sphere, Himalaya Mountain with Himalaya Mountain,
Sineru with Sineru, till they are broken to bits and disappear.
vsm2.13:62.1: The wind takes possession from the earth up to the plane of the third jhāna.
vsm2.13:62.2: There, after destroying three Brahmā-worlds, it stops at the Vehapphala-world.
vsm2.13:62.3: When it has destroyed all formed things in this way, it spends itself too.
vsm2.13:62.4:
Then all happens as already described in the way beginning, “The upper space is all
one with the lower space in a vast gloomy darkness …” (§42).
vsm2.13:62.5: But here the world begins its reappearance with the Subhakiṇha Brahmā-world.
vsm2.13:62.6: And beings falling from the Vehapphala Brahmā-world are reborn in the places beginning with the Subhakiṇha Brahmā-world.
vsm2.13:63.1:
Herein, the period from the time of the great cloud heralding the aeon’s destruction up
till the ceasing of the aeon-destroying wind is one incalculable.
vsm2.13:63.2:
That from the ceasing of the wind up till the great cloud of rehabilitation is the second
incalculable … These four incalculables make up one great aeon.
vsm2.13:63.3: This is how the destruction by wind and reconstitution should be understood.
vsm2.13:64.1: What is the reason for the world’s destruction in this way?
vsm2.13:64.2: The three roots of the unprofitable are the reason.
vsm2.13:64.3: When any one of the roots of the unprofitable becomes conspicuous, the world is destroyed accordingly.
vsm2.13:64.4: When greed is more conspicuous, it is destroyed by fire.
vsm2.13:64.5: When hate is more conspicuous, it is destroyed by water
vsm2.13:64.6: —though some say that it is destroyed by fire when hate is more conspicuous and by water when greed is more conspicuous.
vsm2.13:64.7: And when delusion is more conspicuous, it is destroyed by wind.
vsm2.13:65.1: Destroyed as it is in this way, it is destroyed for seven turns in succession by fire and the eighth turn by water;
vsm2.13:65.2:
then again seven turns by fire and the eighth turn by water; then, when it has been seven times
destroyed by water at each eighth turn, it is again destroyed for seven turns by fire.
vsm2.13:65.3: Sixty-three eons pass in this way.
vsm2.13:65.4:
And now the air takes the opportunity to usurp the water’s turn for destruction, and in destroying the world
it demolishes the Subhakiṇha Brahmā-world where the life span is the full sixty-four eons.
vsm2.13:66.1:
Now, when a bhikkhu capable of recollecting eons is recollecting his former lives, then of such eons as these he recollects
many eons of world contraction, many eons of world expansion, many eons of world contraction and expansion.
vsm2.13:66.2: How? In the way beginning, There I was …
vsm2.13:66.3:
Herein, There I was: in that eon of contraction I was in that kind of becoming or generation
or destiny or station of consciousness or abode of beings or order of beings.
vsm2.13:67.1: So named: such forenames as Tissa, say, or Phussa.
vsm2.13:67.2: Of such a race: such family names as Kaccāna, say, or Kassapa.
vsm2.13:67.3: This is said of the recollection of his own name and race (surname) in his past existence.
vsm2.13:67.4:
But if he wants to recollect his own appearance at that time, or whether his life was a rough or refined one, or whether
pleasure or pain was prevalent, or whether his life span was short or long, he recollects that too.
vsm2.13:67.5: Hence he said with such an appearance … such the end of my life span.
vsm2.13:68.1: Here, with such an appearance means fair or dark.
vsm2.13:68.2: Such was my food: with white rice and meat dishes as food or with windfall fruits as food.
vsm2.13:68.3:
Such my experience of pleasure and pain: with varied experience of bodily and mental
pleasure and pain classed as worldly and unworldly, and so on.
vsm2.13:68.4: Such the end of my life span: with such a life span of a century or life span of eighty-four thousand eons.
vsm2.13:69.1:
And passing away from there, I reappeared elsewhere: having passed away from that becoming, generation,
destiny, station of consciousness, abode of beings or order of beings, I again appeared in that other becoming,
generation, destiny, station of consciousness, abode of beings or order of beings.
vsm2.13:69.2:
And there too I was: then again I was there in that becoming, generation, destiny,
station of consciousness, abode of beings or order of beings.
vsm2.13:69.3: So named, etc., are as already stated.
vsm2.13:70.1: Furthermore, the words there I was refer to the recollection of one who has cast back retrospectively as far as he wishes,
vsm2.13:70.2:
and the words and passing away from there refer to his reviewing after turning forward again; consequently,
the words I appeared elsewhere can be understood to be said with reference to the place of his reappearance
next before his appearance here, which is referred to by the words I appeared here.
vsm2.13:70.3:
But the words there too I was, etc., are said in order to show the recollection of his name, race,
etc., there in the place of his reappearance next before this appearance.
vsm2.13:70.4:
And passing away from there, I reappeared here: having passed away from that next place of reappearance,
I was reborn here in this khattiya clan or brahman clan.
vsm2.13:71.2:
With its aspects and particulars: with its particulars consisting in name and race;
with its aspects consisting in appearance, and so on.
vsm2.13:71.3: For it is by means of name and race that a being is particularized as, say Tissa Kassapa;
vsm2.13:71.4: but his distinctive personality is made known by means of appearance, etc., as dark or fair.
vsm2.13:71.5: So the name and race are the particulars, while the others are the aspects.
vsm2.13:71.6: He recollects his manifold past lives: the meaning of this is clear.
vsm2.13:71.7: The explanation of the knowledge of recollection of past lives is ended.
